author: Pierre-MarieMarchio
name: .NET Clean Architecture API
description: A .NET 10 HTTP API on Clean Architecture, meant to be kept: a domain, use cases, infrastructure modules behind ports and a thin presentation layer, on EF Core with PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite (for development), with architecture tests, CI and its own documentation. Local accounts, an external OpenID Connect provider or no authentication; the hosts it holds (the HTTP API, a Blazor portal, an MCP server, a desktop app, a worker), Files, the example features and a first web app are options.

choices.description: The supplied Auth module: local accounts, JWT access and refresh tokens, its own database context.
Accounts held by an external OpenID Connect provider (Keycloak, Entra ID, Auth0...): bearer tokens validated against Authentication:External, each subject mapped to an internal owner.
No accounts: every endpoint is public. Leaves out the example features and the Files module.
Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

choices.description: PostgreSQL: a schema per feature, the row's xmin as its version, advisory locks for the leases.
SQL Server: a schema per feature, a version counter the save stamps, application locks for the leases.
SQLite, for development only: one file, a table prefix per feature, in-process leases; the API refuses to start outside Development.

database.description: The database the project runs on. The project only carries this one.

developmentConnectionString.description: The Default connection string of appsettings.Development.json, for the chosen database and the credentials .env.example gives it.

templateMaintenance.description: Never true in a generated project. Names the pieces that maintain the template itself - the acceptance matrix, the test-count floor, the tree-auditing gates, the changelog - so they stay in the template repository only.

templateVersion.description: The template package's version, which release-please raises, read by .template.config/TemplatePackage.csproj and recorded in a generated project's overview; its release is tagged v<version>.

files.description: Include the Files module: stored files, their storage adapters, the object-store container and the Files tables of the business context.

choices.description: TodoLists, Reminders and Notes.
Notes only: the simple example, with no domain model and no other feature to lean on.
No example feature: the modules, the mechanisms and their tests only.

examples.description: Which example features the project starts with. Reminders needs TodoLists, so they come together.

ci.description: Include the GitHub Actions workflows that build, test, scan and release the solution (ci.yml, codeql.yml, release.yml; web.yml with a web app).

sonar.description: Include the Sonar analysis: the local SonarQube compose profile, its scanner image and task, and the SonarQube Cloud workflow when --ci is true.

agentFiles.description: Include AGENTS.md, the brief for coding agents and people, and src/Web/AGENTS.md with a web app. It is the only agent file the template writes.

agentFilesExample.description: With --agent-files true, the closing section of AGENTS.md, the one this project's team writes, ships with example lines about a made-up product instead of empty prompts: each line marked Example, to replace or delete.

aspire.description: Include an Aspire app host beside Docker Compose: src/AppHost starts the containers Compose runs and every host cleanarch.json records, with the settings Compose gives them and their telemetry in the Aspire dashboard. Compose stays the reference of the deployment.

choices.description: Not an option to set: it names the refusal.

aspireNeedsServerDatabase.description: Never set. The app host runs each host as a process on this machine, and the SQLite shape keeps its file in the volume Compose shares between containers, which those processes cannot share: choose --database postgresql or sqlserver, or leave out the app host with --aspire false.

choices.description: The HTTP API, <Project>.Api: versioned routes, OpenAPI, the reference the clients are written from. Comes with any web app, desktop client, or MCP server under local accounts, which call it.
A Blazor Web App with server interactivity, <Project>.Portal, created by dotnet new blazor and calling the use cases in process.

An MCP server, <Project>.Mcp, written in the shape of dotnet new mcpserver --transport remote, whose tools call the use cases in process for the caller its access key or its provider's token names. Needs --auth local or external.
An Avalonia desktop app, <Project>.Desktop, created by dotnet new avalonia.mvvm and calling the API through the .NET client in src/Presentation.

A WPF desktop app for Windows, <Project>.Desktop, written in the shape of dotnet new wpf, calling the API through the .NET client in src/Presentation; Windows first: developed, run and tested on Windows, while other systems build it and the tasks name the tests they skip.
A worker, <Project>.Worker, written from the shape of dotnet new worker, that runs the background jobs the API runs otherwise. Needs a server database.

presentation.description: The presentation projects the project holds, one or several: each is a host of the use cases in src/Presentation, created at bootstrap by its framework's own generator or written whole. A server host reaches the application layer in process, a client reaches the API through the .NET client. Pass the option once per project; a project adds one later with dotnet new cleanarch-presentation.

needsWorker.description: True when the project holds neither the API nor the worker, so that no host would run the background jobs without the worker.

jobsWorker.description: True when the worker runs the background jobs, chosen or added for a project without the API, which runs them otherwise.

anyPresentation.description: True when the project holds a presentation project of its own beyond the API and the worker, which docs/features/presentation.md describes.

accessKeys.description: True when local accounts have an MCP server to call: brings the access keys its callers present, their routes, table, tests and decision.

dotnetClient.description: True when the project holds a presentation or a web app that calls the API through the .NET client in src/Presentation. Brings the client, its tests, the api-client task and the Kiota tool.

postActions.description: Bootstrap the project before anything else.

manualInstructions.text: In the project folder, run dotnet tool restore, then dotnet cleanarch bootstrap, and commit what it writes: the tests, verify and the stack assume it ran. The restore installs the tools .config/dotnet-tools.json pins, dotnet cleanarch among them; bootstrap formats the usings around the project's name, writes the OpenAPI reference and creates each context's initial migration. It needs the network, not Docker. dotnet new creates no git repository: run git init before the first commit. dnx CleanArch.Create -- new --setup does the git init, the commits, bootstrap and the .env copy in one go.
